papers.protocol_caution: The paper has conflicting hyperparameter prose/table descriptions (batch sizes and NFEEG learning rate). Do not copy these details into our text; no need to correct or rely on them. Resting spectral correlations are not equivalent to prospective biomarker or mechanistic validation.

papers.safe_related_work_claim: BEETL extended evaluation across subjects and heterogeneous MI datasets while providing labelled target-subject calibration examples. Its protocol therefore illustrates cross-dataset transfer under target adaptation and is not a matched source-only comparator for our frozen external evaluation.
papers.inclusion_recommendation: Suitable benchmark/protocol-context citation; never present its calibration-assisted accuracy as directly comparable to our no-target-fit balanced accuracy or assert superiority.

candidate_related_work_paragraph: Transfer-learning studies often permit adaptation using target-subject data. Zhang et al. proposed target-subject fine-tuning of pretrained CNNs [candidate identity: Zhang2021AdaptiveTransfer], and the BEETL motor-imagery challenge supplied labelled calibration examples for its target participants [Wei2022BEETL]. These protocols differ from the present frozen source-only evaluation, which prohibits target fitting and target-driven model selection. The present contribution is an audit of source-only selection, participant-level heterogeneity and complete-pipeline transfer, rather than a new domain-generalization algorithm or a claim of superiority over adaptation methods.
candidate_physiology_context_sentence: Resting-state alpha/beta associations with participant-specific decoding have also been investigated in unilateral elbow imagery [Sonntag2025Neurophysiological]. Our BNCI-only nine-person characterization uses baseline-relative sensor-level task power after decoder outcomes are fixed; it is neither a prospective predictor nor evidence of a learned decoder mechanism.
